title: WPSS/675/2021 of JAI LAXMI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH SECRETARY PWD DEHRADUN

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No.675 of 2021
Jay Laxmi ........Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others .....Respondents
Presence:-
Mr. M.C. Pant, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. Pradeep Hairiya, learned Standing Counsel for the State.
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J. (Oral)

The writ petition has been filed by the petitioner
challenging the order dated 06.08.2020, passed by
respondent no.4, whereby the claim of the petitioner for
compassionate appointment has been rejected and further
for a direction to the respondents to give appointment to
the petitioner under Dying in Harness Rules treating the
petitioner as a dependent of her late father with all
consequential benefits.
2. It is the case of the petitioner that father of the
petitioner was working with the respondent-department as
Beldar who died on 13.03.2019, while still in service,
leaving behind two daughters i.e. one the present
petitioner (a married daughter) and the other younger one
named as Monika. The petitioner being married daughter
of the deceased employee Mr. Balram has moved an
application for compassionate appointment on
04.03.2020. The said application of the petitioner was
rejected vide order dated 06.08.2020, passed by
respondent no.4, annexure-1 to the writ petition, saying
therein that there is no provision in the statute to give
appointment to a married daughter of a deceased
government servant under Dying in Harness Rules, 1974
known as the U.P. Recruitment of Dependants of

2
Government Servants Dying In Harness Rules, 1974 (as
adopted by the State of Uttarakhand in the year 2002).
3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the
petitioner that the State Government vide notification
dated 04.09.2019 has amended the Dying In Harness
Rules, 1974 and by this amendment, in the definition of
Family in Rule 2(c), Sub-Clause (3) was substituted by
word "daughter". Earlier clause 3 read as "unmarried
daughters, widow daughters and divorcee daughters". He
further submits that vide amendment which was brought
in the statute vide notification dated 04.09.2019, the
controversy has set to rest by inserting word "daughter" in
the definition of Family given under Dying in Harness
Rules, 1974. Thus, according to him, there is now no
scope to get confuse as to whether the married daughter
or unmarried daughter will be included in the definition of
family. Now "daughter" includes both.
4. Learned State Counsel does not dispute the fact
with regard to the insertion of the "daughter" in the
statute and according to that, at present, married
daughter is also entitled to get appointment on
compassionate ground. But, according to learned State
counsel the caveat is that the married daughter should be
dependent upon the deceased government servant as
enunciated in the Full Bench judgment passed by this
Court in Special Appeal No.187 of 2017 and batch decided
on 25.03.2019 (Udham Singh Nagar District Cooperative
Bank Ltd. & another vs. Anjula Singh and Others).
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner admits that
the ratio of the judgement rendered by the Full Bench as
mentioned hereinabove speaks about the pre-condition of

3
married daughter being dependent upon the deceased
government employee. But it is argued by him that in the
case in hand, petitioner has submitted an affidavit on
18.12.2021 stating therein on oath that the petitioner was
dependent upon her father as her husband is not gainfully
employed.
6. This Court heard the matter on 02.04.2024
and on that date, learned State Counsel was directed to
seek instructions in the matter as to whether the
petitioner could be offered appointment in view of the
amendment incorporated vide notification dated
04.09.2019 under Dying in Harness Rules or not.
7. Pursuant to the said direction, the written
instruction dated 06.04.2024 has been received and
supplied to this Court and in the instructions, it has been
categorically stated that there is no objection from the side
of the respondent to give appointment to the petitioner on
compassionate ground under amended Dying in Harness
Rules dated 04.09.2019. The said instructions are taken
on record.
8. In view of the written instructions received by
this Court as well as the affidavit dated 18.12.2021 which
has been submitted by the petitioner before the authority
concerned, this Court is of the opinion that the petitioner
was dependent upon deceased government servant i.e. her
father and the husband of the petitioner is not gainfully
employed.
9. In this view of the matter, the order dated
06.08.2020 is hereby quashed and the writ petition is
allowed. A mandamus is issued to the competent
authority-respondent no.4 to consider case of the

4
petitioner afresh for appointment on compassionate
ground, in the light of the observation made in the body of
this judgment, by speaking and reasoned order, within a
period of eight weeks from the date of production of
certified copy of this order
10. No order as to costs.
11. Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 09.04.2024
AK
